The Problem

Most businesses don't lose work because people aren't interested.

They lose it when confidence collapses after interest, under decision pressure. It usually looks like plenty of activity with no predictable outcome, results that swing month to month with nobody able to explain why, and advice to add more: more ads, more posts, more spend. Nobody tells you what's actually broken.

That isn't a tactics problem. It's a confidence problem. And it happens in a small number of specific places, which is the useful part: if there are only a few places it can break, you can go find out which one it is instead of guessing.

That's the first thing I do. Not execution. Not a campaign. Identifying where confidence is collapsing between interest and decision. Once that's clear the correction is usually straightforward. Until it's clear, everything else is guessing.

The Four Moments

There are only a few places a sale can break.

Nearly every revenue problem I see comes down to one of four moments.

Not Seen When the Decision Is Made

You weren't there when they decided.

People were looking for what you do. You just weren't in front of them at the moment they picked somebody.

Seen But Not Trusted

They found you and didn't trust you yet.

They looked, and they left. The interest was real. The confidence wasn't.

Trusted But Still Compared

They trusted you and shopped you anyway.

You gave the estimate, they compared, and you lost some you should have won, usually on price, because the difference between you and the other fellow never got made clear.

Selected But No Action

They meant to hire you and never got to it.

They said they'd call back, and they meant it. Most of those jobs aren't lost. They're stuck.

Different problems, different fixes, and the fix for one does nothing for the other three.

Here's the trouble. From where you sit, you can only see one of the four. You know about the estimates you lost. You don't know about the people who never came back, never called, or never found you at all.

More advertising doesn't fix lost demand.
Finding the failure point does.

The Demand Collapse Diagnostic™ looks at all four, not by asking you to guess, but by reading what your own numbers already say: where you land when somebody nearby is choosing, what people do on your site before they leave, what they type before they hire, and who came looking and never called.

After the Launch

We catch it before it costs you.

Campaigns don't fail loudly. They fail quietly, in ways you'd never see on an invoice. Every account gets watched every week. Recent catches:

  • A plumbing client's campaign delivery collapsed 90% overnight. Caught the same day, diagnosed as a campaign issue, not a market issue, and restored. Conversions never dipped.
  • An email campaign started silently dropping one in four sends. Caught before the next send went out, fixed before the client ever saw it.
  • Visitors on three client sites were clicking buttons that didn't respond, at the exact moment they were trying to act. Found it in the behavior recordings. Fixed it.

The launch is the easy part. The watching is what you're paying for.

Questions

Is the plan really free?

Yes. Qualified companies in available territories receive the plan without paying for it. You keep the plan whether you implement it yourself or ask Marketing Performance Group to help.

Why do I have to qualify?

Every plan is researched and prepared for a specific company and market. The review is designed for established home-service companies where the findings can support a meaningful recovery plan.

Is the scorecard the complete diagnosis?

No. The twelve questions identify the first failure point to investigate. The personalized review examines the company, market, competitive position and available evidence before the plan is prepared.

Do I have to hire Marketing Performance Group afterward?

No. The plan is yours. You may implement it yourself. If you want Marketing Performance Group to implement it through EngageEngine™, that conversation happens only after you have seen the plan.

What information do you need?

The application asks for basic company information, your website, trade, service area and current challenge. Robbie begins with publicly available information and the answers you provide. Any request for additional access should be explained and approved separately.

What if my territory is already claimed?

Marketing Performance Group works with one company per trade, per market. If a direct competitor has already claimed the territory, Robbie will tell you before preparing the full plan.

How is EngageEngine™ different from ordinary advertising?

Ordinary advertising usually starts with channels and budgets. EngageEngine™ starts with the confirmed failure point, applies buyer-signal intelligence to the local market and coordinates the work around where demand is actually being lost.
